# coder_foundation (Data Source)

This proposed POC data source requires the companion development provider and
matching Coder server support. It is not a released provider feature. A Foundation
owns shared infrastructure independently of its attached templates.

In a Foundation run, this data source identifies the Foundation itself. In a
workspace build, it identifies the attached Foundation and exposes the supplied
immutable outputs snapshot. It makes no API calls and does not read live Terraform
state. All attributes are computed; there is no ID argument for selecting another
Foundation or snapshot. `snapshot_id` identifies the run that produced the supplied
snapshot, not necessarily the current Foundation run.

Use `coder_template` for template identity. A Foundation ID is not a template ID.
Preserve existing identifier inputs on live resources: changing a resource name
from a template ID to a Foundation ID can replace infrastructure.

## Example usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    coder = {
      source = "coder/coder"
    }
  }
}

provider "coder" {}

# Coder resolves the current Foundation automatically in both provisioning scopes.
data "coder_foundation" "current" {}

locals {
  # A snapshot might not be available during template import.
  subnet_ids = try(data.coder_foundation.current.outputs.subnet_ids, toset([]))
}

output "foundation_id" {
  value = data.coder_foundation.current.id
}

output "snapshot_id" {
  value = data.coder_foundation.current.snapshot_id
}

# Public outputs stay usable in for_each even when the snapshot contains secrets.
resource "terraform_data" "subnet" {
  for_each = local.subnet_ids
  input    = each.value
}

output "subnet_ids" {
  value = local.subnet_ids
}

output "token" {
  value     = try(data.coder_foundation.current.sensitive_outputs.token, null)
  sensitive = true
}
```

`outputs` contains only non-sensitive root outputs. `sensitive_outputs` contains
only sensitive root outputs and is always marked sensitive, even when empty.
Both objects come from the same pinned snapshot and preserve exact Terraform
types, including sets, lists, maps, tuples, typed nulls, and arbitrary-precision
numbers. A sensitive root output's entire value belongs to `sensitive_outputs`,
including any nested objects or collections.

Public maps and sets of strings can be used in `for_each` without `nonsensitive`,
even when the snapshot also contains secrets. Consume secrets through
`sensitive_outputs`, not `outputs`. Terraform outputs that expose secrets must
declare `sensitive = true`. Sensitive values remain in Terraform state; protect
state storage and access.

Each object is empty when the snapshot has no outputs in its sensitivity category.
When no snapshot is supplied, both objects are empty. Use `try` with an
appropriate fallback for optional outputs, including during template import.
A direct reference to an absent key produces Terraform's standard missing-attribute
error. The provider cannot customize that expression error without also breaking
valid fallback expressions. Coder supplies a pinned snapshot; Terraform determines
whether required outputs are available.

## Environment contract

| Variable | Attribute | Missing or empty fallback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CODER_FOUNDATION_ID` | `id` | `import` |
| `CODER_FOUNDATION_NAME` | `name` | `default` |
| `CODER_FOUNDATION_TEMPLATE_IDS` | `template_ids` | `[]` |
| `CODER_FOUNDATION_SNAPSHOT_ID` | `snapshot_id` | Empty string |
| `CODER_TEMPLATE_OUTPUTS` | Values for both output objects | `{}` |
| `CODER_FOUNDATION_OUTPUT_METADATA` | Types and sensitivity for both output objects | `{}` |

Foundation and snapshot IDs must be UUIDs when nonempty. Template IDs must be a
JSON array of UUID strings. An unbound Foundation has an empty template list.
Missing Foundation metadata never falls back to template identity.

`CODER_TEMPLATE_OUTPUTS` is a JSON object mapping root output names directly to
values, not the envelopes returned by `terraform output -json`. For every output,
`CODER_FOUNDATION_OUTPUT_METADATA` must contain the matching key with `type` in
Terraform's JSON type format and a boolean `sensitive` flag. For example:

```text
CODER_TEMPLATE_OUTPUTS={"subnet_ids":["subnet-a","subnet-b"],"token":"secret"}
CODER_FOUNDATION_OUTPUT_METADATA={"subnet_ids":{"type":["set","string"],"sensitive":false},"token":{"type":"string","sensitive":true}}
```

This exposes `outputs.subnet_ids` and `sensitive_outputs.token`. The environment
transport remains a single values object with a matching metadata object.

The two environment objects must have exactly the same keys. Nonempty values
without metadata are rejected rather than guessing types or sensitivity. JSON
null is not an empty snapshot; use `{}` for both variables. Invalid or incomplete
metadata, duplicate keys, and values that do not match their types fail the entire
read without publishing either output object. Errors do not include output
values. Coder must supply the values and metadata before starting
Terraform and keep them immutable for the entire invocation, including schema
requests, validation, planning, and applying.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the Foundation, or `import` when no Foundation metadata is available. Never falls back to the template ID.
- `name` (String) Name of the Foundation, or `default` when unavailable.
- `outputs` (Dynamic) Object containing only non-sensitive Foundation outputs with their exact Terraform types. Can be used in for_each without nonsensitive. Defaults to an empty object when no non-sensitive outputs are supplied; use `try` for optional outputs.
- `sensitive_outputs` (Dynamic, Sensitive) Sensitive object containing only sensitive Foundation outputs with their exact Terraform types, from the same pinned snapshot as outputs. Always marked sensitive, including when empty. Defaults to an empty object when no sensitive outputs are supplied; use `try` for optional outputs.
- `snapshot_id` (String) UUID of the Foundation run that produced the supplied outputs snapshot, or an empty string when unavailable. This metadata does not select a run.
- `template_ids` (List of String) IDs of templates attached to the Foundation, or an empty list when unbound or unavailable.
